news.title: BMC clears removal of 126 trees for Powai SRA project; developer to provide 4,000 PAP homes
news.para: The BMC Tree Authority approved removing 126 trees for a Powai slum rehabilitation project.  This decision followed the developer's commitment to provide over 4,000 free rehabilitation flats.  Officials surveyed the site and identified 144 trees, with 126 affected by construction.  The authority permitted felling 44 trees and transplanting 82 others.  This new approval supersedes an earlier one due to redevelopment layout changes.

news.title: Chandigarh reviews online tenancy portal ahead of launch
news.para: Chandigarh administration reviewed an online Tenancy Portal for upcoming rules.  The portal will facilitate registration of tenancy agreements and UIN generation.  It aims to formalize the rental housing sector and resolve disputes efficiently.  Officials were directed to ensure the portal is user-friendly and accessible.  The new tenancy rules are expected to streamline rental processes for residents.

news.title: Bhubaneswar civic body to intensify action against building plan violations ahead of SC hearing
news.para: Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation will activate enforcement squads to address building plan deviations.  This action follows Supreme Court scrutiny over unauthorized constructions nationwide.  The civic body will submit an action taken report to the apex court soon.  Inspections will identify violations like extra floors and encroachments on setbacks.  The move aligns with Supreme Court directives on building compliance and regulatory issues.

news.title: Credai suggests double verification of soil reports after tilted tower incident in Bengaluru
news.para: Credai-Karnataka now suggests double verification of soil investigation reports for developers. This advisory practice follows a recent incident involving a tilted apartment tower in Bengaluru. The developers' body aims to minimize errors in critical soil assessment for structural design. Homebuyers are also urged to select only credible and registered developers for their projects. Accurate geotechnical investigations and strict adherence to engineering standards are now emphasized.

news.title: Ghaziabad: RWAs yet to file power audit reports, 307 societies get notices
news.para: Ghaziabad power department issued notices to 307 housing societies for mandatory electricity audit reports.  These audits verify common-area power consumption and prevent resident overcharging by societies.  Most societies failed to submit reports, prompting fresh 15-day notices with penalties.  Non-compliance may lead to fines and disconnection of electricity connections for defaulting societies.  The department is monitoring all distribution zones and will take action in early August.

news.title: Bombay HC quashes PMLA case against D B Realty, its managing director
news.para: Bombay High Court quashed a money laundering case against D B Realty and Vinodkumar Goenka. This criminal proceeding was linked to the Maharashtra Sadan construction controversy involving Chhagan Bhujbal. The court accepted arguments that transactions did not constitute proceeds of crime. The Enforcement Directorate had not challenged discharge orders for other parties in the case. This ruling effectively ends the money laundering allegations against the company and its director.

news.title: SC slams CBI, Delhi Police EoW over silence in Indiabulls probe, calls their conduct 'shocking'
news.para: The Supreme Court criticized investigative agencies for their silence on Indiabulls Housing Finance allegations. The court expressed shock at the lack of progress and a perceived quid pro quo situation. Agencies were directed to file a status report within two weeks regarding the investigation. Previous court orders had urged the CBI to finalize its decision on registering regular cases.

news.title: Haryana cabinet cuts stamp duty, registration fee for EWS beneficiaries
news.para: The cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, approved a sharp reduction in stamp duty and registration charges for Economically Weaker Section (EWS) beneficiaries purchasing eligible dwelling units of up to 60 square metres.

news.title: CM seeks 11.56 lakh PMAY-G houses for Telangana from centre
news.para: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy requested Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan for 11.56 lakh houses. He highlighted the state's housing priorities and the previous government's failures. A survey identified over 11 lakh eligible rural families needing homes. Reddy also sought expanded rural development works due to deficient rainfall. This expansion aims to improve livelihoods and promote crop diversification for vulnerable groups.

news.title: Bombay high court grants interim relief to SD Corporation in defamation suit
news.para: The Bombay High Court granted interim relief to SD Corporation regarding defamatory social media posts.  The court ordered that allegedly damaging content should not be circulated further.  SD Corporation alleged false and misleading posts targeted its MHADA redevelopment project.  The developer sought damages and an injunction against further publication of such material.  The court will hear the matter again on August 31, 2026.

news.title: Indian cities need $2.4 trillion investment by 2050: Report
news.para: Indian cities will need about $2.4 trillion of investment by 2050 to become climate-resilient and low-carbon, according to a FICCI-EY report. Only 20 municipal corporations have accessed capital markets so far, raising about $476 million.

news.title: Maharashtra: Housing societies get sweeping governance reforms, approved bylaws become binding
news.para: Maharashtra's amended cooperative housing rules cut minimum members for new societies to five, make model bylaws automatically applicable, curb arbitrary levies and ease redevelopment, succession and parking disputes

news.title: Shiva Cement gets approval for 2.4 MTPA dolomite mining in Odisha
news.para: Shiva Cement has received modified environmental clearance and consent to operate for its Khatkurbahal North limestone and dolomite mine in Odisha. The approval allows the company to commercially mine and sell 2.4 million tonnes of dolomite annually.

news.title: Ambuja Cements' net profit falls 37% to ₹660 crore in Q1 FY27
news.para: Ambuja Cements reported net consolidated profit after tax of ₹660 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with ₹1,041 crore in Q1 FY26. Its net consolidated total income declined to ₹9,669 crore during the quarter.

news.title: Knowledge Realty Trust’s net operating income rises 15% to ₹1,111.7 crore in Q1 FY27
news.para: Knowledge Realty Trust reported consolidated total income of ₹1,268.14 crore and net profit of ₹250.79 crore. Its manager approved a distribution of ₹751.63 crore, or ₹1.695 per unit, for the quarter.

news.title: NGT bars brick kiln, stone crusher in Assam’s Nalbari until clearances, CTO obtained
news.para: The National Green Tribunal has stopped brick and stone crusher units in Nalbari. Both units must obtain statutory clearances and follow environmental norms. The tribunal issued this order after complaints about riverbed violations. Joint committee reports confirmed units were not operational during inspection. District authorities will examine elephant corridor objections and ensure compliance.

news.title: Lloyds Realty leases 1.82 lakh sq ft office tower in Mumbai to Smartworks
news.para: Lloyds Realty Developers has leased the entire 1.82 lakh sq ft of The Square in Andheri East, Mumbai, to Smartworks for 15 years. The transaction is expected to generate rental revenue of over ₹600 crore during the lease tenure.

news.title: As many as 74 ‘highly dangerous’ buildings in Vasai-Virar ordered to be vacated immediately
news.para: Vasai Virar Municipal Corporation has ordered residents of seventy-four dangerous buildings to vacate immediately.  This directive comes amid ongoing monsoon rains and concerns about structural integrity.  A recent survey identified these buildings as unsafe for habitation and owners received notices.  The civic body will not be responsible for any mishaps if directives are not followed.  Residents are urged to shift to safer locations without any further delay.

news.title: BMC panel to decide fate of 3,169 trees for Dharavi redevelopment & infrastructure projects in Mumbai
news.para: Mumbai's Tree Authority will consider proposals impacting 3,169 trees on Tuesday.  Permissions are sought to fell 1,777 trees and transplant 1,392 others for development.  The Dharavi redevelopment project seeks to remove 1,693 trees, with compensatory planting planned.  Other projects include a tunnel, IIT housing, and a slum rehabilitation scheme.  These decisions come amid growing scrutiny over tree removal for infrastructure.

news.title: Mumbai: BMC panel to consider leasing 15-acre Mulund dump land for Dharavi redevelopment works
news.para: The BMC plans to lease fifteen acres of reclaimed land at Mulund dumping ground. This land will be used by Dharavi Redevelopment Project for a casting yard. The civic body expects to earn over one hundred crore rupees in rent. The developer will manage site remediation and obtain necessary environmental clearances. This proposal will soon be presented for approval by the Improvement Committee.
